tex_parallel_compile.note: tex_file_writing.py: module-global ThreadPoolExecutor (_get_tex_compilation_pool, max_workers = cpu count) with a Future registry keyed by the absolute hash-named SVG path (_tex_compilation_futures). The synchronous tex_to_svg_file joins a same-key in-flight job, so submit-all then construct-synchronously is the intended pattern. tex_mobject.py MathTex.precompile submits per-formula jobs whose cache paths exactly match later MathTex(...) constructions; graph.py Graph.__init__ already precompiles default vertex labels this way. Fork boundary: _try_start_cairo_fork_job calls _shutdown_tex_compilation_pool_for_fork, which refuses while futures are in flight, forcing serial fallback for that play. Measured on this fork: 16 distinct cold formulas 120.7 s sequential vs 11.7 s submit-all/collect; 7 cold Graph labels 24.662 -> 4.760 s (docs/research/perf-evidence.md).

cairo_fork_gate.note: cairo_renderer.py: _cairo_fork_pipeline_is_requested (int workers >= 2, os.fork present, sys.platform == linux, parent partial-movie stream never opened), _cairo_fork_pre_begin_is_eligible / _cairo_fork_post_begin_is_eligible (exact CairoRenderer + Camera, plain .mp4 with libx264, writer without sounds or open streams, scene without foreground/scene updaters/meshes/always_update_mobjects/stop_condition, trusted mobject families, per-animation lifecycle audit), _cairo_fork_animation_type_is_supported (exact-type allowlist; composition containers audited recursively), _cairo_fork_transform_scope / _cairo_fork_creation_scope (rate_func accepted by identity, path_func must be transform.py _RENDER_PLAN_STRAIGHT_PATH; Write and Indicate accept their own exact defaults, creation.py _CAIRO_FORK_TRUSTED_WRITE_RATE_FUNC = linear and indication.py _CAIRO_FORK_TRUSTED_INDICATE_RATE_FUNC = there_and_back), and _try_start_cairo_fork_job (joins the idle TeX pool, requires main thread with threading.active_count() == 1). Monotonic disable: _begin_parent_cairo_animation sets _cairo_fork_permanently_disabled the first time a written play opens the parent encoder, so later eligible plays cannot fork; cached (skipped) plays do not open it. workers 0..1 means unrequested, not blocked. cairo_fork_workers bounds in-flight forked plays (_prepare_cairo_fork_slot). Measured at 1080p: Bayes 7.55 -> 3.95 s, Algorithm 12.13 -> 7.50 s (docs/research/perf-evidence.md).

cairo_static_layers.note: cairo_renderer.py: save_static_frame_data builds a z-ordered layer plan when cairo_static_layers is set and the play spans >= 3 frames (the experimental cairo_compositor variant needs >= 8); _build_cairo_static_layer_plan plus _cairo_static_layer_inputs_are_trusted gate it (exact CairoRenderer/Camera, standard writer handoff methods, opaque RGBA background without background_image, every animation scope recognized via _cairo_animation_scope, trusted mobject families). Static runs above moving objects are cached as transparent surfaces and composited per frame, so a dynamic object early in the display order no longer forces the static suffix to re-raster (MLP209 severity input). A frozen static Wait deliberately keeps the legacy single-frame path. Opt-in trade-off per default.cfg: tiny antialias rounding differences at static/dynamic layer boundaries.

cairo_bulk_interpolation.note: cairo_renderer.py: _try_arm_cairo_bulk_interpolation_recipes arms packed per-play point/style interpolation after the first canonical frame; constants _CAIRO_BULK_MIN_FRAMES = 12, _CAIRO_BULK_MIN_FAMILY_COUNT = 4, _CAIRO_BULK_MIN_AMORTIZATION = 192 (effective member floor is max(4, ceil(192 / (frames - 2)))). Every animation of the play must be exactly Transform or _MethodAnimation (the .animate builder) with lag_ratio 0, reverse_rate_function False, rate/path funcs accepted by identity (animation.py _RENDER_PLAN_TRUSTED_RATE_FUNCTIONS = (linear, smooth); transform.py _RENDER_PLAN_STRAIGHT_PATH), disjoint live families, and no updaters anywhere in the scene's mobject families; the static-layer input gate must also pass. Gated-out plays keep canonical frames-by-family-by-channels interpolation cost. Measured: 300 members / 60 frames interpolation 130.658 -> 33.004 ms/play, steady state 2.0761 -> 0.1890 ms/frame (docs/research/perf-evidence.md).

svg_cache.note: svg_mobject.py: module-global SVG_HASH_TO_MOB_MAP keyed by hash_obj(SVGMobject.hash_seed) = (class name, svg_default, path_string_config, file_name, config.renderer). SVGMobject.init_svg_mobject(use_svg_cache=True) stores a deep copy on miss and serves hits as deep copies, so per-construction cost never reaches zero; entries are never evicted, so frame-varying keys in hot callbacks grow the map O(F) for the life of the process (MLP217). The map also exists upstream; this overlay declares the semantics so profile-gated rules can rely on it.

continuous_movie_stream.note: scene_file_writer.py: _continuous_movie_stream_is_safe merges uncached Cairo plays into one encoder stream — per-play partial-movie boundaries disappear — only for an exact SceneFileWriter over an exact CairoRenderer with disable_caching = True, no sections, sounds or transparency, plain .mp4, and standard writer methods. MLP210's per-play partial-stream cost term applies only when OutputState actually shows per-play streams.

config_keys.name: cairo_fork_workers
config_keys.note: default.cfg: Linux-only fork-per-play Cairo pipeline; 0 disables, enabled values must be >= 2.

config_keys.name: cairo_static_layers
config_keys.note: default.cfg: opt-in faster Cairo compositing; can introduce tiny antialias rounding differences at layer boundaries.

config_keys.name: cairo_compositor
config_keys.note: default.cfg: experimental moving-layer compositor reusing a reference raster for narrowly audited translations; requires >= 8 frames per play.

config_keys.name: cairo_compositor_fades
config_keys.note: default.cfg: group-alpha compositing for audited FadeIn/FadeOut translations; intermediate frames are not pixel-identical to per-object fades.

config_keys.name: cairo_antialias
config_keys.note: default.cfg: one of constants.py CAIRO_ANTIALIAS_MODES (default | fast | none); fast/none trade edge quality for faster rasterization.

config_keys.name: video_encoder
config_keys.note: default.cfg: one of constants.py VIDEO_ENCODERS; auto probes hardware encoders with a real two-frame encode and falls back to libx264. Any value other than libx264 (auto included) blocks the Cairo fork pipeline.

config_keys.name: x264_preset
config_keys.note: default.cfg: one of constants.py X264_PRESETS, ordered fastest to slowest.

config_keys.name: opengl_pbo_readback
config_keys.note: default.cfg: experimental movie-only asynchronous OpenGL readback; submission order is verified at runtime with synchronous fallback.

config_keys.name: opengl_pbo_depth
config_keys.note: default.cfg: delayed readback buffer count; enabled values must be >= 2.

fork_capabilities.note: Curated by hand from a private Manim fork working tree (base commit 4d25c031 plus optimizations that are not published); this overlay is therefore not independently reproducible and is never the default profile; every fact cites the gate function or config file it was read from and is reviewer-verified, not generator-extracted. Fast-path interpretation is local-fork-overlay only: upstream_0_20 lacks this block entirely, keeping MLP214/MLP225 and cairo_fork_workers / cairo_static_layers fast-path semantics inert there (DESIGN 7.3). Calibration numbers quoted in notes are machine-specific evidence (docs/research/perf-evidence.md), never portable truth.

manim.constants.CAIRO_ANTIALIAS_MODES.note: Fork-only: Cairo image-backend antialias modes; absent from upstream 4d25c031.

manim.constants.VIDEO_ENCODERS.note: Fork-only: accepted `video_encoder` names; absent from upstream 4d25c031.

manim.constants.X264_PRESETS.note: Fork-only: libx264 preset names; absent from upstream 4d25c031.

manim.mobject.text.tex_mobject.MathTex.p.note: Fork-only classmethod (tex_mobject.py MathTex.precompile): submits several independent formulas for parallel TeX compilation and returns list[Future[Path]] immediately; keyword options mirror the constructor so each cache path exactly matches a later MathTex(...) construction, which joins the same in-flight job.

manim.utils.tex_file_writing.tex_to_svg_.note: Fork-only (tex_file_writing.py tex_to_svg_file_async, in tex_file_writing.__all__ but not star-exported from manim/__init__.py): non-blocking TeX compile plus dvisvgm conversion returning Future[Path]; same-key jobs coalesce process-wide and an existing SVG yields an already-resolved future.
